newsitem.title: USA: CME to list Mexican CETES/TIIE contracts in April.
newsitem.headline: CME to list Mexican CETES/TIIE contracts in April.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said it would launch futures and options on Mexican Treasury bills (CETES) April 3 and on the Mexican Equilibrium Interbank Interest Rate (TIIE) April 17.

"The ability of Mexican entities to trade these short-term interest rates is a real boon which we foresee as helping to build liquid markets from the start," CME president Rick Kilcollin said in a statement.
"Mexican banks and investment houses are natural participants in CETES and TIIE futures and options trading," he said.

The CETES futures, sized at two million pesos per contract, will be based on the 91-day Certificados de la Tesoreria de la Federacion, which are discount treasury bills similar to U.S. Treasury bills, CME said.

The TIIE futures, sized at six million pesos, will be based on the 28-day Tasa de Interes Interbancario de Equilibrio, a rate determined by the Banco de Mexico at which supply and demand for wholesale bank loans are in equilibrium.
Regular trading hours will be 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Chicago time.
The CETES and TIIE contracts will trade alongside peso derivatives and other Mexican contracts on CME's Growth and Emerging Markets division.
"Now the Merc offers one-stop shopping for Mexican short-term interest rates, Brady bonds, the peso and the IPC Mexican stock index," CME chairman Jack Sandner said in the statement.
